sections.html:
West Springfield sits in Hampden County on the west bank of the Connecticut River, directly across from Springfield, which is why locals call it the West Side. The city bills itself as the Crossroads of New England. It covers 17.54 square miles, 16.73 of them land, and had 28,835 residents in the 2020 census. Hartford is about 27 miles away and Boston about 90.

The Westfield River runs along the southern side, and East Mountain, a ridge of volcanic trap rock that is part of the Metacomet Ridge, forms the western boundary. West Springfield became a town in 1774 and a city in 2000, and it has a mayor-council government.

This is a city of named districts rather than one downtown: Amostown, Ashleyville, Cayenne, Downtown (also called Center), Memorial, Merrick, Mittineague and Tatham. Memorial surrounds Memorial Avenue and the Big E fairgrounds, Ashleyville sits near I-91 and Riverdale Street, and Mittineague lies on the north bank of the Westfield River.

The Eastern States Exposition, known as the Big E, began in 1917 and is the city's biggest tourist draw. The former Eastern States Farmers' Exchange headquarters now serves as West Springfield Town Hall.

sections.h2: A short look at the past
sections.html:
Settlers farmed good land on the west bank, and market gardening grew around Riverdale Road from the 1830s. The Western Railroad arrived in 1841, and for decades rail yards in Mittineague and near Memorial Avenue made the railroad one of the largest employers. Paper mills lined the Westfield River, including Southworth Paper, Agawam Paper and Strathmore. Holyoke split off in 1850 and Agawam in 1855, which is why the city's map looks smaller than its colonial territory.

That mix of farm, rail and mill history explains the variety of housing, from older houses near the center to later builds near the highways. Describe your own house by its age and updates.

Water and weather are part of this city's past, and buyers and insurers ask about them. The Westfield River flooded the town in 1936, when 8,000 people were displaced out of about 17,000. Hurricanes Connie and Diane brought floods in 1955, five days apart. Dikes now protect low neighborhoods.

  • On June 1, 2011, a tornado touched down in West Springfield before crossing into Springfield.
  • On October 29, 2011, a wet snowstorm brought down limbs and wires, and some homes waited more than a week for power.

If your house is near the river or the dikes, gather any flood insurance records and repair receipts. Those papers answer the first questions a buyer will ask. Look at the FEMA flood map and your policy for your exact address.

Snow and ice hit roofs and trees hardest. Before listing, walk the property with these in mind:

  • Look for ice-dam stains on ceilings and along exterior walls.
  • Check large limbs that hang over the roof or service lines.
  • Test the sump pump if the basement is below the neighborhood grade.

A buyer paying cash may skip these fixes and adjust the price, which can be simpler than repairing a house you plan to leave.

sections.h2: How roads and buses connect the city
sections.html:
Interstate 91 crosses the northeast part of town, the Massachusetts Turnpike (I-90) passes through, and U.S. 5 (Riverdale Street), U.S. 20 (Westfield Street) and Route 147 (Memorial Avenue) run through it. Pioneer Valley Transit Authority buses link the city to Springfield and to Westfield State University, and Amtrak serves Springfield.

The city has no airport. Bradley International in Windsor Locks, Connecticut, is the nearest with commercial flights. Highway access is a real selling point for a commuter, and highway noise is worth mentioning honestly if your street is close to the ramps.

West Springfield follows the state process. You can seek an abatement when the assessed value is higher than fair cash value, meaning the price a willing buyer and seller would agree on without pressure, or when an exemption or classification is wrong.

  • The valuation date is January 1 before the fiscal year starts on July 1.
  • Apply to the assessors by the first payment due date shown on your bill.
  • The assessors have three months to answer, and silence counts as denial.
  • Appeal to the Appellate Tax Board within three months after that.

Ask the city's assessors and collector which installment schedule applies to your bill and where to find the form.

sections.h2: What a seller pays at closing
sections.html:
ChargeAmountNotes
Deed excise tax$4.56 per $1,000 of taxable valueCounts any fraction of $1,000; no tax when the stated price is under $100
Deed recording fee$155Hampden County Registry of Deeds; cash or checks
Municipal lien certificate$80Small charge that shows the scale of other items

The seller usually pays the deed excise tax. Other closing items, such as a payoff, title work and a municipal lien certificate, depend on the property, and your closing attorney can itemize them.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants or storm damage
sections.html: Occupied and damaged houses sell too. With tenants, read the lease first, share its terms early, and ask any buyer in writing how the tenancy will be handled. With flood or storm damage, say plainly what happened, what was repaired and what remains, and keep the insurance records and receipts together. A buyer who pays cash may take the house as it stands, and the offer will reflect the work still to do.

sections.h2: What to gather before you talk to buyers
sections.html:
1. Your latest tax bill and the installment schedule printed on it.
  2. Flood insurance records, repair receipts and any sump or dike-related paperwork if you are near the river.
  3. Lease copies and rent details if tenants live there.
  4. Payoff information for any mortgage or lien.
  5. Your closing attorney's contact details.

Unpaid taxes and liens are normally settled out of the proceeds at closing, so knowing the amounts early lets you judge any offer on what you would actually keep.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a West Springfield house quickly
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer from an investor. Listing works well when the house is in good shape and you can wait out showings and a buyer's financing. A cash offer fits when the house has deferred repairs, flood or storm damage, tenants or probate issues.

Whichever route you pick, ask for the contract in writing, check who pays closing costs, and confirm that the buyer can show proof of funds before you commit.

faqs.q: Why is West Springfield called the West Side?
faqs.a: It lies on the west bank of the Connecticut River, across from Springfield. Early residents had to cross the river by boat to reach Springfield's meetinghouse.

faqs.q: How much is the deed excise tax in Hampden County?
faqs.a: The registry lists the rate as $4.56 per $1,000 of taxable value or fraction of $1,000. There is no tax when the stated price is under $100.

faqs.q: Is West Springfield in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of it have flooded repeatedly, including in 1936 and 1955, and dikes now protect low areas. Check the FEMA flood map and your insurance records for your exact address.

faqs.q: What is the Big E and where is it?
faqs.a: The Big E is the Eastern States Exposition, a fall fair that began in 1917 on grounds near Memorial Avenue. It is the city's largest tourist attraction.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Springfield house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers, including cash buyers, purchase occupied homes. Read the lease and the Massachusetts tenant guidance first, and ask the buyer in writing how they will handle the tenancy.
